Modified assessment incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):

- Policy stance: The May 1 FOMC is a hawkish hold—solid growth and low unemployment but “lack of further progress” on inflation keeps cuts on hold. Slowing QT (Treasury cap from $60B to $25B; MBS cap steady at $35B) is a modestly dovish nod to market functioning.

- SLOOS overlay: Banks report broad tightening and weaker demand across categories:
  • C&I and consumer/credit card/auto: tighter standards and terms, higher loan spreads, increased credit score requirements, tighter credit limits, and weaker loan demand. 
  • CRE: widespread tightening—wider spreads, smaller loan sizes, lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, shorter interest-only periods, and narrower market areas—driven by concerns over rents, vacancy rates, and property prices (notably office).
  • Cited reasons include economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, industry-specific problems, liquidity position, supervisory/legislative/accounting changes, competition, and secondary market conditions.

- Synthesis: While the FOMC notes a “better balance” of risks, SLOOS indicates a meaningful tightening in bank credit supply alongside softer loan demand, pointing to downside risks for activity and credit-sensitive sectors. This reinforces vigilance on inflation but also rationalizes the QT slowdown. Net tone shifts from cautiously neutral to modestly negative.
